newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Offshore strength sparks Australian stocks at open.
newsitem.headline: Offshore strength sparks Australian stocks at open.

text.p: Australian shares strode ahead at the open on Thursday, the market marching to the tune of record breaking finishes in offshore markets.
The All Ordinaries index climbed 19.5 points to 2,665.9.
Brokers said the early gains had been inspired by the Dow advance through the 8,000 barrier and while a strong finish was anticipated, some profit-taking later would not surprise.
"New York going through 8,000 had them looking pretty good and that's flowed through to here," said a dealer at a Sydney-based brokerage.
"But you may well see them give something back later on."

Bellwether BHP added 20 cents to A$18.39, while the gold sector added 1.4 percent, largely on a modest three cent rise to A$1.55 from sector heavyweight Normandy Mining, and strong showings from Gutnick-controlled companies Centaur Mining and Exploration NL and Australian Gold Resources.
They both added over 10 percent to A$1.60 and 95 cents respectively after rumours of an imminent bid for Great Central Mines Ltd, the largest Gutnick firm.
Brokers said the interlocking nature of shareholdings in the mining entrepeneur's stable of companies meant their prices often moved in tandem.

Great Central, the centre of bid speculation with Canadian giant Barrick Gold Corp, was two cents higher at A$2.73 after hitting an early high of A$2.812, 34 percent higher than last week's low of A$2.10 during the sell-off which followed the tumble in gold prices to 12 year lows.
Great Central's Jundee neighbour in Western Australia Eagle Mining NL was a big performer, albeit on modest volumes, climbing 20 cents to A$2.35.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about seven to two, while about 41 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
